chapter: Early listening, piano and adolescent conflict
title: Girls, loneliness and a boyhood between church and street
summary: Interested in girls but conflicted, he felt accepted by neither his father's world nor the street, with churches beside gambling and pool halls.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What period? When you were 16 and 17 you mean?
Yes, going up into that period, which when I started going with the girls --
I was just going to say you started to say you'd like to --
Yes, this was next.
-- take the occasional girl out.

Yes, you see, all of this has to do with my learning to decide for myself or becoming -- wanting to decide for myself. I became interested in girls, I remember my first little girl friend that I decided I wanted to take out to the show. And I was a little bashful and so forth, you know. One of those things in your life that everybody goes through during the same time.
Yes.
And I didn't feel that I was too successful at this, and I don't know, I think you might say in that period I maybe elected to sort of be a loner, because of all of this atmosphere, this --
Conflict.

Conflict of interest. Wanting to be congenial and accepted by the outer public, but yet being sheltered and disciplined at home; you see, this was a conflict in my life, you see. And it was hard for me to deal with that as a child, see, because even the people, when they came to church they would mind their manners and everything, but most people when they went to church in those days, they'd come into church and as soon as they'd leave the church they'd take off their tie and take off their shoes, and sit down with a beer or some scotch and soda, or a home brew, or
corn liquor, whatever. And forget about all that.
But you see, I was under this all the time, you see.
Yes.
And so this conflict was there, and I didn't have too much ambition to try things like other people. I think perhaps I was somewhat discouraged, you might say, because it was like --
You were handicapped.

Right, it was a handicap for me. Not -- in other words I just -- I think I had a feeling of not being wanted, or not being accepted in either side. Not wanting to be as my father wanted me to be, and not knowing whether I was wanted on the other side. See. But as I grew up -- now, because of this, because of the environment, of people around me, as I said, my father would have a church on one corner in many instances, and on the next corner or the opposite corner there probably could be a house of ill repute.
Yes.
Or a gambling establishment. You know?
Yes.
Or a pool hall.
Yes.
